entities.evidence: The Cain who leaves here is Eve’s son and Abel’s brother, whom Yahweh addressed after Abel’s death.
The divine name identifies the God who addressed Cain and whose presence Cain now leaves. The source tag LORD refers to the same bearer as the earlier Yahweh proposal.
The phrase “in the land of Nod” names the territory where Cain settled and locates it east of Eden.
“East of Eden” locates Nod relative to the Eden where Yahweh God planted the garden in Genesis 2:8.

review.translation: [Then|0] [Cain|1] [went out|0] [from the presence of|2] [Yahweh|3] [and settled|4] [in the land of|5] [Nod|6], [east of|7] [Eden|8].

analysis.evidence: Cain is the subject of וַיֵּצֵא. The phrase מִלִּפְנֵי יַהְוֶה identifies whose presence he left, and the next clause says he settled in the land of Nod.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־
analysis.sense: go out, depart from a place or someone’s presence

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for Cain with its etymology left open pending evidence.
draft.definition: Cain, the son of Adam and Eve and brother of Abel.
draft.evidence: Genesis 4:1 names Eve’s son קַיִן. Genesis 4:2 identifies Abel as his brother and names Cain again when describing his work.

analysis.evidence: In וַיֵּצֵא קַיִן מִלִּפְנֵי יַהְוֶה, קַיִן names the subject who went out from Yahweh’s presence. The same subject carries over to וַיֵּשֶׁב, describing Cain’s settlement in the land of Nod.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: The personal name of Abel’s brother.

analysis.evidence: In וַיֵּצֵא קַיִן מִלִּפְנֵי יַהְוֶה, לִפְנֵי יַהְוֶה identifies Yahweh’s presence, and the prefixed מִן marks it as the place Cain left.
analysis.morphology: Prefixed מִן with its נ assimilated to ל, followed by לִפְנֵי (לְ + פְּנֵי, plural construct of פָּנִים).
analysis.sense: before, in the presence of (a person, Yahweh)

analysis.evidence: In וַיֵּצֵא קַיִן מִלִּפְנֵי יַהְוֶה, “Cain went out from the presence of Yahweh,” the name identifies the one whose presence Cain left.
analysis.morphology: Proper noun, singular, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

analysis.evidence: Cain is the subject of both וַיֵּצֵא and וַיֵּשֶׁב. After he leaves Yahweh’s presence, בְּאֶרֶץ נוֹד identifies the land of Nod as the place where he settled.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־
analysis.sense: to take up residence in a place

analysis.evidence: In וַיֵּשֶׁב בְּאֶרֶץ נוֹד, Nod names the territory where Cain settled. The phrase קִדְמַת עֵדֶן locates it east of Eden.
analysis.morphology: Preposition בְּ ‘in’ prefixed to a common noun in the singular construct.

analysis.evidence: In בְּאֶרֶץ נוֹד, “in the land of Nod,” נוֹד names the land where Cain settled. קִדְמַת עֵדֶן, “east of Eden,” locates it geographically.
analysis.morphology: Proper noun of place, singular, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In קִדְמַת עֵדֶן, the construct form קִדְמַת takes עֵדֶן as its complement and locates the land of Nod east of Eden.

draft.change: Add a place-name word for עֵדֶן alongside the identically pointed noun meaning delight.
draft.definition: Eden is the place where Yahweh God planted a garden.
draft.evidence: Genesis 2:8 locates the garden with the phrase גַּן בְּעֵדֶן, “a garden in Eden.”

analysis.evidence: Cain settled in the land of Nod. The phrase קִדְמַת עֵדֶן, “east of Eden,” uses Eden as the geographic reference point for Nod.
analysis.morphology: Singular proper noun without prefix or suffix, in the absolute state after the construct form קִדְמַת.
analysis.sense: Eden, the place where Yahweh God planted a garden.
